text:
B: Hi. Laura.
A: Hi, Gemma. You're Chineham, aren't you? Gillian said.
B: Yes, by the lakes. Are you too?
A: Yeah, the newer bit. I walk the dog round the lakes most mornings.
B: Oh, I've probably seen you, then. Cocker spaniel?
A: Dexter. If you saw one covered in fox poo this morning, that was him.
B: Ha. No, I missed that. So what do you do?
A: New car sales. The franchise on the retail park. You?
B: Management accountant, logistics. I do the monthly accounts and budgets for three depots.
A: Oh, numbers. Do you enjoy it?
B: I do, actually. I like month-end when it all ties up. I've got a checklist I've been tweaking for six years. Sounds a bit sad, I know.
A: No, that's how you get things right. I've got a lad at work who can't fill in a finance form without three goes. I'd kill for someone with a checklist.
B: I'd be happy to lend it you. I'm not sure it'd cover car finance, though.
A: Ha. Do you want to go further? Financial controller or whatever?
B: Erm, maybe. In a few years. I'm not desperate. Alfie's six, so I want to keep it sensible.
A: I'd just go for it. If you're the one getting it right, make sure they know it. People like you get overlooked because you don't shout.
B: Maybe. I don't really like shouting, to be honest.
A: You don't have to shout. Just put it in front of them.
B: Yeah. Fair point. Erm, what does your husband do?
A: Craig's an electrician. Self-employed.
B: No way. So's Dan. He runs a little business with one other bloke.
A: Seriously? Craig might know him. What's the business called?
B: Just his surname, really. Dan Hollis Electrical. Very imaginative.
A: I'll ask him. They all end up in the same builders' merchant anyway.
B: Probably Darren's.
A: Ha, probably. Have you got any other kids?
B: Erm, no. Just Alfie. You?
A: No. Just the dog. And a garden room Craig's been building since about March.
B: Dan's been meaning to do our fence since spring. I've given up asking.
A: Give him a deadline. Works with Craig. Sort of.
B: Ha. Do you run? You look quite sporty.
A: Gym mostly. I did the Basingstoke Half once. Two hours four.
B: Oh, well done. I just do parkrun. War Memorial Park. I'm on eighty-seven.
A: Eighty-seven? That's a lot of Saturdays.
B: It is. I want to get to a hundred, then I get the t-shirt.
A: What's your time?
B: About thirty-one minutes. I'm not quick.
A: Eighty-seven, though. That's consistency. That's worth more than speed, to be fair.
